name: Canthal tilt theory

lead: Canthal tilt is the angle of the line joining the inner and outer eye corners relative to horizontal. In looksmaxxing, a positive tilt (outer corner higher) is read as sharper, more alert and more masculine, and many users aim for that look.

Tilt is set by the position of the eye corners, which are anchored by the canthal tendons and the shape of the bony orbit. Surgeons and researchers measure it routinely, and studies of pageant winners and attractiveness have reported tilt values, but no large trial establishes it as a principal driver of attractiveness. Makeup and lash styling change how tilt appears without altering anatomy.

paras: Most people start by measuring tilt from a straight-on photo, then use eyeliner, lash styling, brow shaping or hairstyle to change the impression. Some discuss posture, midface support or surgical options such as canthoplasty, which clinicians perform on the outer corner.

Measuring tilt carries no risk. Canthoplasty, canthopexy, filler and orbital or midface surgery are medical procedures with ordinary surgical risks, and some forum do-it-yourself approaches are ones clinicians would not endorse. Community threads also link the concept to distress for users who see a negative tilt as decisive.

chain: Eyes read as sharper, more alert
angle.text: Forum users measure the angle of the eye corners and treat a positive tilt as a marker of a sharper, more attractive eye area, with makeup, styling or surgery used to change how it reads. The tilt itself is measurable; the strong rule built on it has had little direct testing.

lead: Canthal tilt is the angle between a horizontal line and the line joining the inner corner (medial canthus) and outer corner (lateral canthus) of the eye.[1][2] In looksmaxxing slang a positive tilt means the outer corner sits higher than the inner corner, a neutral tilt means they are level, and a negative tilt means the outer corner sits lower.[3][4] It is one of the most frequently cited eye-area metrics in the subculture, alongside 'hunter eyes', a term Wikipedia defines as a positive canthal tilt with little upper-eyelid exposure and low-set brows.[4]

The theory's appeal for appearance is practical: tilt is read from a photograph, and several of the things that change how it reads are accessible and reversible. Eyeliner and mascara placement, brow shape and height, lash length, leanness of the face, lighting and camera angle all alter the apparent line of the eye. Members who want a lasting change discuss surgery, usually lateral canthoplasty or canthopexy, performed by clinicians. Proponents say a more upward tilt makes a face look alert, energetic and sexually dimorphic; Grokipedia reports the community view that a negative tilt can read as tired.[3]

Outside the community, canthal tilt is a standard measurement in plastic surgery, ophthalmology and craniofacial research. A 2007 experiment found judges preferred female faces with a digitally exaggerated medial canthal tilt, and later cross-sectional studies in Italian, Asian and Western samples have found higher attractiveness ratings associated with more upward-inclined eye fissures.[5][6] Reports in newspapers and magazines have documented how looksmaxxing forums and TikTok creators turned the measurement into a rule of thumb, and that this rule has not itself been tested in a trial.[4]

paras: The canthi are the two corners where the upper and lower eyelids meet. The outer corner is sharper and the lids lie close to the eyeball there, while the inner corner extends toward the nose and encloses a small triangular space.[1] The two ends of the palpebral fissure define the axis whose angle from horizontal is the canthal tilt; in cephalometric work the landmarks are called the endocanthion and exocanthion.[1][2]

Tilt is determined by where the canthal tendons attach to the bony orbit and by the soft tissue of the lids, cheek and brow. Because the lateral canthal tendon attaches to the outer orbital rim, surgeons who adjust it can change the angle, and aging, midface descent and lid laxity can alter how the angle looks.[7][8]

In many East Asian, Southeast Asian and other populations the epicanthic fold covers part of the inner corner. Wikipedia describes it as a skin fold of the upper eyelid that is common among East and Southeast Asian people and nearly universal in Japan and South Korea.[9] Because the fold hides the inner landmark, clinicians sometimes distinguish a tilt measured to the visible inner corner from one measured to the true medial canthus, and surgical papers on epicanthoplasty discuss how the region affects the look of the upper eyelid.[9]

Researchers usually measure tilt from standardized photographs or 3D images. A 2024 cross-sectional study of 145 Caucasian patients with dermatochalasis used 3D photogrammetry to record canthal tilt alongside other eyelid dimensions; it found that tilt did not differ significantly by sex, while several lid-width measurements declined with age.[2]

A study of 21 beauty-pageant winners from Kyrgyzstan, using the corneal diameter as a scale, reported a mean canthal tilt of 9.0 degrees (plus or minus 2.0) among 26 distances, 9 angles and 16 indices.[10] A cross-sectional measurement study of 76 Korean patients with a mean age of about 23 reported a mean canthal tilt of roughly 8.4 degrees.[6]

A 3D imaging comparison of 46 Asian and 101 Caucasian young adults found ethnic and sex differences in eyelid and canthal measurements, with the largest differences in canthal tilt and fissure dimensions.[6] Because values depend on head position, lighting, which landmarks are used, and population, figures from different studies are not always directly comparable.

Looksmaxxing began in the 2010s in incel and manosphere communities. Wikipedia reports that three now-defunct forums, PUAHate, Sluthate and Lookism.net, known together as the PSL forums, generated much of the vocabulary and the PSL rating scale, and that TikTok creators popularised the term in the 2020s.[4] Canthal tilt and hunter eyes entered that vocabulary as part of rating the 'eye area'. Wikipedia cites Business Insider, Vice and The Guardian coverage in 2023 and 2024 describing men pursuing hunter eyes through mewing, rubbing the orbital area or surgery.[4]

Looksmax.org holds many threads on the topic, for example asking whether tilt can be raised, whether a negative tilt can be changed without surgery, or whether eyeliner can fake it.[11][12][8][13][14] The streamer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, is among the figures Wikipedia links to the more extreme mid-2020s phase of the culture, which was covered in The New York Times, The Guardian and GQ in February 2026.[4]

Researchers have also begun to write about the phenomenon. A 2026 editorial in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Global Open discussed looksmaxxing and male beauty standards and their ethical implications for plastic surgery.[6]

The 2007 study by Bashour and Geist in Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery is the paper most often cited in forum and encyclopedia discussions. Judges using experimental software chose between unmodified female faces and versions edited in Photoshop to exaggerate medial canthal tilt, and preferred the accentuated faces in about 93 percent of trials; the authors suggested the cue relates to neotenic and sexually dimorphic features.[5] The study concerned female faces, so it does not directly address the claim as stated for men.

A 3D morphometric study of 199 ordinary and 126 'attractive' Italian young adults reported that attractive subjects had a narrower distance between the inner corners, longer eye fissures and greater fissure inclination.[6] A 2023 analysis of 100 AI-identified landmarks in 42 Caucasian celebrities found that attractive women had a greater canthal tilt than men, with no sex difference in fissure length.[6] A 2026 cross-sectional study of 3,517 Asian adults from a public face database, with AI-derived attractiveness scores, reported that higher-rated faces had a larger outer canthal angle and canthal tilt along with smaller brow-to-lid and intercanthal distances.[6]
These studies are observational or use edited images, and they relate tilt to attractiveness ratings among other eye measurements; none tests tilt as the sole or principal determinant.

No studies found that test canthal tilt theory itself, meaning a trial showing that tilt alone determines attractiveness in men or that a given intervention improves ratings of attractiveness. Related research uses canthal tilt as a measured outcome in surgery and as one variable in attractiveness studies.
See the section on the research base above: one edited-image experiment in female faces and several cross-sectional studies associate a more upward tilt with higher ratings.[5][6]

In a 2023 comparison of two operations for unilateral coronal craniosynostosis, distraction patients showed significantly better postoperative symmetry in canthal tilt than a matched cohort treated with advancement and remodeling.[15] A 2024 retrospective comparison of 20 patients treated by endoscopic-assisted versus open distraction also tracked canthal tilt symmetry, with gains in the endoscopic group.[16] A review of facial feminization surgery noted that patients undergoing brow lift and eyelid surgery had a higher rate of negative canthal tilt at baseline.[17]

Studies in aesthetic surgery have reported tilt change after lateral procedures: in one 2026 retrospective series of 22 Asian women lateral canthal tilt rose from 2.1 to 4.3 degrees at six months and settled at 3.6 degrees at 12 months, and in an 85-patient East Asian series of lateral hooding correction it rose by about 5 degrees.[6] These are uncontrolled retrospective reports from clinics, performed for ptosis or hooding correction rather than for the looksmaxxing goal.

The surgical literature on lateral canthoplasty describes the procedure mainly to correct or prevent lower eyelid malposition, with outcomes studied in retrospective series.[7] Wikipedia notes that canthoplasty is performed for both cosmetic and functional reasons.[18]

sections.h: Methods people discuss for changing tilt
paras: General categories mentioned in community threads include makeup and eyeliner, lash trimming, exercises, mewing, bone-smashing, and surgery such as canthoplasty or canthopexy.[11][12][8] Posters frequently report that eyeliner and brow styling change the apparent line, while others report that eye exercises gave only temporary results.[12]
No controlled study has shown that mewing or facial exercises change canthal tilt. Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article states that mewing lacks evidence of altering facial structure.[4]

Surgeons describe soft-tissue approaches as well, such as lateral canthal suspension and lifts of the lateral brow or temple that change the visible angle.[6] These are clinical procedures and their candidacy and risks are decided with a surgeon.

Users post photos for tilt assessment, argue over whether tilt is mainly bone structure or soft tissue, and sometimes describe a negative tilt as a serious disadvantage. Others in the same forums argue that the concept is overweighted or that eye-area appeal depends on other traits such as eyelid exposure, brow position and under-eye support.[11][12][8]

Grokipedia reports that the community also ties tilt to leanness, noting that low body fat can sharpen the eye contours.[3] Wikipedia describes the PSL scale and related vocabulary as pseudoscientific according to researchers and critics, which is the context in which the tilt rule circulates.[4]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, canthal tilt is discussed as a core eye-area metric and a frequent source of advice and anxiety threads.[11][12][8]

claims.claim: A positive canthal tilt is a key marker of male attractiveness.
Mewing or tongue posture can raise canthal tilt by moving the upper jaw and cheeks.
Tilt cannot be changed without surgery.
Eyeliner, lashes and brow shaping can change how tilt looks.
Hunter eyes combine positive tilt, deep-set eyes and little upper-lid exposure.
A negative canthal tilt makes a man's outcomes hopeless.
Tilt means the same thing across ethnic groups.

timeline.event: Bashour and Geist report that judges preferred female faces with exaggerated medial canthal tilt in about 93 percent of trials.[5]
Incel and manosphere forums, the PSL sites, build the vocabulary (PSL, mogging, hunter eyes) in which canthal tilt becomes a core metric.[4]
A 3D study of 199 ordinary and 126 attractive Italian adults reports greater fissure inclination in the attractive group.[6]
A retrospective review of lateral canthoplasty techniques describes procedures mainly for lower eyelid malposition.[7]
Business Insider, Vice and The New York Times cover looksmaxxing and hunter eyes as it spreads on TikTok; studies of pageant winners and craniosynostosis surgery report tilt measurements.[10][15][4]
A 3D photogrammetry study in 145 dermatochalasis patients records canthal tilt by age and sex; The Guardian covers looksmaxxing.[2][4]
A cross-sectional study of 3,517 Asian adults links larger canthal tilt with higher AI attractiveness scores; a plastic surgery editorial discusses looksmaxxing ethics.[6]
